crossConcepts.reason: The primary complex-conjugate conditions yield roots 2±i and t±i. Polynomial factorization is then needed to express P(1) as the product of the four (1−root) values, giving 2((1−t)²+1); without that bridge the coefficient sum is not obtained. Quadratic minimization is separately needed to choose t=1 (allowed by t≠−2) and get the minimum coefficient sum 1. Neither operation is contained in merely determining the conjugate roots.
